LanguageData.RimLogic_LogicBlock.label: logic block
LanguageData.RimLogic_LogicBlock.description: A universal logic block. Types include AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR, splitter, and more. Use the Type button to switch between researched types.
LanguageData.RimLogic_FunctionalBlock.label: functional block
LanguageData.RimLogic_FunctionalBlock.description: A universal functional block. Types include switch, selector, math block, multitool, and more. Use the Type button to switch between researched types.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Sensor.label: sensor
LanguageData.RimLogic_Sensor.description: A universal sensor. Types include light, motion, temperature, power, pollution, fire, and more. Use the Type button to switch between researched types.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Diode.label: diode
LanguageData.RimLogic_Diode.description: Lets power flow only in one direction: from input to output while the input side has surplus energy, and opens the circuit when it does not. A control signal on the input turns the diode on or off, and the output sends a signal when power is actually passing through.
LanguageData.RimLogic_SignalGenerator.label: signal generator
LanguageData.RimLogic_SignalGenerator.description: Keeps a signal on the output while enabled. A basic constant “one” source for circuits. Can be controlled by a logic input. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_TickGenerator.label: tick generator
LanguageData.RimLogic_TickGenerator.description: Outputs regular signal pulses. Can be controlled by a logic input. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Register.label: register
LanguageData.RimLogic_Register.description: Each new signal on the input inverts the output. Keeps its state. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Timer.label: timer
LanguageData.RimLogic_Timer.description: Delays a signal. When it receives a signal on the input, it repeats it on the output after the configured delay. Useful for pauses and timed sequences. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Memory.label: memory
LanguageData.RimLogic_Memory.description: Stores a number. A normal signal stores 1 or 0, while blocks that carry numbers (selector, math block, another memory block) pass their value through. Memory keeps that number until the next change. It has a default value set in settings. When the value changes, it sends a pulse on the output. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Screen.label: screen
LanguageData.RimLogic_Screen.description: Shows one digit of the number coming into its input. Several screens connected to the same source form a display: the first connected screen shows ones, the second shows tens, and so on. Negative numbers add a minus sign. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Clock.label: clock
LanguageData.RimLogic_Clock.description: Outputs a signal at the chosen time of day. In settings, choose an hour or a range of hours and a condition (before, after, within range, and so on). While the local time matches it, the output has a signal. Requires power.
LanguageData.RimLogic_Loudspeaker.label: loudspeaker
LanguageData.RimLogic_Loudspeaker.description: When it receives a signal, it shows an in-game notification — blue or red — with your own title and text. Useful when a sensor or circuit should report an event by itself. The signal also passes through to the output. Requires power.
